points.text: High circuit errors mean variance of unfaithful circuits is weak evidence against EAP-IG
Wording like 'critical vulnerability' overreaches the evidence
No other discovery method (ACDC, edge pruning) as reference for high variance
No random-edge null model or expected Jaccard under sampling noise
Greedy connectivity-based sizing confounds Jaccard; no fixed-size or matched-faithfulness control
Edge overlap a debatable notion; equal-error different circuits suggest non-identifiability
Deval equals D, so circuit error is in-sample
Dataset size, replicate count and seeds not given in main text
Bootstrap effectively smaller data; more stable meta-dataset results weaken message
Bootstrap validity for discrete selection undiscussed; no CIs or tests on stability numbers
Datasets are templated, so effective diversity is small
Different estimators need not agree; framing as sensitivity is weak
Median circuit over rows varying along different axes is arbitrary
Degenerate rows like size-1 circuits included in averages
Table 1 averages incommensurate regimes and degenerate cases
IG steps, number of edges and threshold not varied
Noise experiment only covers GPT-2 on two tasks
Fixed-direction embedding noise unmotivated; scale depends on embedding norm
Greater-Than error high across noise range; claim unsupported
No evidence noise instability predicts bootstrap instability or transfer failure
GPT-2 vs Llama comparison confounded by size, tokenization and faithfulness
Instruction tuning conclusion based on one pair in unfaithful regime
Reading multimodal Jaccard as distinct stable solutions is speculative; no clustering
Sensitivity and non-identifiability already documented in prior work
No estimand, bias analysis, confidence sets or proposed method
Single method family, small models, three templated tasks, yet broad claims
No demonstration that bootstrap Jaccard changes conclusions about published circuits
Table 1 discussion appears twice nearly identically
Table references wrong in places, including noise results
Claims like no tighter clustering in Fig. 1 lack quantitative support
Repeated paragraph on p.7 indicates lack of care, possible other errors
Undefined abbreviation, repeated paragraphs, caption placement, wrong Table/Figure reference
EAP-IG is a first-order approximation, so circuit variance is unsurprising
Number of samples used for attribution scores not reported
Focus solely on circuit discovery despite broad interpretability framing
Other methods like Path Patching, Edge Pruning, Information Flow Routes neglected
No dedicated limitations section
Claim that circuits fail to transfer is unsupported and contradicted by prior work
Interpretability proxy metric description incomplete
Experimental intervention noise procedure insufficiently described
Which model produced Table 1 not specified
Instruction tuning finding consistent with prior work, which should be cited
Circuit error very high; EAP poorly calibrated; stability should be at fixed error
Without identifiability, parallel pathways and self-repair make stability uninformative
Identifiability depends on ablation method; circuits across variations may not be comparable
Instability may be artifact of discretization and Jaccard; analyse scoring separately
Experimental setup details lacking
Analysed circuits largely unfaithful; should threshold error and compare sizes
Comparing errors ignoring circuit size is misleading

P.summary: Central claim rests on unfaithful high-error circuits
Overreaching wording about vulnerability
No comparison with other circuit discovery methods
No null model or sampling-noise baseline for Jaccard
Jaccard confounded with circuit size and selection rule
Edge overlap ignores functional equivalence / non-identifiability
Circuit error evaluated in-sample
Dataset size, replicates and seeds unreported
Bootstrap inflates variance; meta-dataset weakens headline
Bootstrap validity and confidence intervals missing
Templated datasets with little diversity
EAP variants are distinct estimators, not hyperparameter sensitivity
Median circuit is an arbitrary reference
Degenerate cases and incommensurate regimes averaged
True EAP-IG hyperparameters not varied
Noise experiment limited scope
Noise design unmotivated and scale non-transferable
'Without harming performance' claim unsupported
Noise-induced instability not shown predictive
Model-size comparison confounded
Instruction-tuning conclusion rests on one pair
Multiple-solutions interpretation speculative
Limited novelty given prior work on sensitivity
Statistical-estimator framing rhetorical
Narrow scope versus broad claims
Recommendations not validated
Duplicated paragraph and wrong table references
Figure claims not backed quantitatively

Q.summary: Analysis focuses on high-error unfaithful circuits
Comparing circuit error while ignoring size is misleading
Lack of attention to detail; presentation errors
Variance finding unsurprising given first-order approximation
Number of samples for attribution unreported
Instability may stem from discretization, not scoring
